issues.description: Method Developer.attend: the problem statement and the template define an instance method attend(course:) that accepts a single optional Course parameter (func attend(course: Course?)). The solution implementation defines attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool) with an extra Boolean parameter, while the solution's Client calls attend(course:) with only one argument. This mismatch (different parameter lists between template/problem and solution, and an inconsistent call site) will cause a compilation error and confuses students about the intended method signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. The simplest fix is to change the solution implementation to match the problem statement and template: declare func attend(course: Course?) { ... } (remove the forCredit parameter) and adjust the implementation body accordingly. Alternatively, if the extra parameter is intentional, update the problem statement, the template signature, and all call sites (e.g., Client) to require and pass the additional Boolean parameter. Prefer keeping the single-parameter signature to preserve the original exercise intent and make the provided solution compile.

issues.description: Concept: the Developer.attend method used to let a Developer attend a Course. Problem statement and template declare a single-parameter method named attend(course:) with signature 'func attend(course: Course?)'. In the solution repository the method is implemented with a different signature 'func attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool)' (an extra Boolean parameter). This signature mismatch means students reading the problem and using the template will implement and call a one-parameter attend(course:) method, but the solution uses a two-parameter variant — creating confusion and a compilation/API mismatch (calls such as myself.attend(course: swiftCourse) will not match the solution's implementation).
issues.suggestedFix: Align the method signatures across artifacts. Preferably change the solution implementation to 'func attend(course: Course?) { ... }' (remove the forCredit parameter) and update the implementation body accordingly so it matches the problem statement and the template. Alternatively, if the extra parameter was intended, update the problem statement and template to require 'func attend(course: Course?, forCredit: Bool)' and update all call sites (e.g., Client.main) to pass the new argument so all artifacts are consistent.
